findings.description: When ANSI stripping is triggered, the code calls `.strip()` on the whole prompt text after `strip_ansi`. This removes leading and trailing whitespace, including the trailing space in prompts such as 'Name: ' and any intentional leading indentation.
findings.rationale: Trigger: a prompt is shown on a non-tty stream or under CliRunner, where `should_strip_ansi` returns True. `strip_ansi(text).strip()` then turns 'Name: ' into 'Name:', so the user's input is typed right against the colon. `echo` strips only ANSI codes and keeps whitespace, so prompt output differs between tty and non-tty streams. Tests that compare prompt output also break.
